figures.finding: Lebanese performers organise in artists' syndicates under Law No. 56/2008 on the organisation of artistic professions: eight syndicates are registered with the Ministry of Culture, each takes applications in its field and files them with the Ministry for approval; members of a syndicate may join the artists' mutual fund (sickness, accident and death allowances, education aid, a retirement pension), funded by members' annual fees, a 2% tax on event tickets, a 10% tax on foreign artists' contracts and a Ministry contribution. No collective agreement or minimum fee was found.

join: apply to the syndicate of one's field
syndicate files with the Ministry of Culture (Directorate of National Cooperation and Coordination) for approval

sources.said: Law No. 56/2008 on the organization of artistic professions was promulgated on 27/12/2008. This law regulates the formation, activity and membership of these syndicates. … Eight artists' syndicates are duly registered in the Ministry of Culture. These syndicates receive membership applications according to their field of work and then file them to the Ministry of Culture - Directorate of National Cooperation and Coordination - for approval after verifying that the required conditions are fulfilled. … This fund accepts memberships after verifying that the required conditions are met, especially that the applicant is a member of a formal syndicate. … Fix a retirement pension for the members. … A tax of two percent on all event tickets (theater, concerts) and all artistic activities … A tax of ten percent on foreign artists contracts collected by the Ministry of Finance and transferred monthly to the fund.

figures.finding: A foreign artist engaged in Lebanon has 10% of the contract taxed for the Lebanese artists' mutual fund, collected by the Ministry of Finance.

sources.said: A tax of ten percent on foreign artists contracts collected by the Ministry of Finance and transferred monthly to the fund.

figures.finding: Arabic is the official national language of Lebanon; the use of French is set by law.

sources.said: Article 11 The Arabic language is the official national language. The conditions under which the French language is to be used are determined by law.

figures.finding: Beirut is Lebanon's capital; no source measuring where most screen work is made was found.

sources.said: Article 4 The Grand Lebanon is a Republic, whose capital is Beirut.
